title: Apply the shared design system to admin-facing pages (follow-up to task 025)
tech: React + TypeScript frontend only -- plain CSS, reusing the shared design system (frontend/src/styles/base.css) established in task 025, no new dependency
keyConstraints: Task 025 built a shared base stylesheet (CSS custom properties for colors/spacing/typography, plus reusable classes -- .page, .card, .btn/.btn-primary/.btn-secondary/.btn-back/.btn-block, .field, [role="alert"], .loading-text) and applied it to the two customer-facing pages. This task extends it across the admin surface, which is currently in two different states, confirmed by reading every admin page: (1) AdminDashboard.tsx, AdminAvailability.tsx (2 classNames total), AdminLoginRequest.tsx, and AdminLoginCallback.tsx have essentially zero styling today -- same starting point BookingWidget/ManageBooking were in before task 025, so these get the same first-time treatment: apply .page/.card/.btn variants/.field/[role=alert]/.loading-text throughout. (2) AdminCalendar.css and AdminServices.css already exist with their OWN hardcoded values from tasks 018/021 that were never reconciled with base.css's tokens -- e.g. AdminServices.css uses #ccc/#f2f2f2 where base.css's --color-border (#d1d5db) and --color-bg (#fafafa) are the near-equivalent shared tokens; these two files should be updated to reference the shared custom properties instead of their own hardcoded hex values, for one consistent palette across the whole app. Exception, do not touch: AdminCalendar.css's booking-status colors (admin-calendar-event-pending/confirmed/blocked -- amber/green/hatched-gray) are a deliberate, distinct semantic language (booking status, not general UI chrome) with their own comment explaining the blocked-vs-booking visual distinction -- these are out of scope for token-reconciliation, though see the open question below about reusing them elsewhere. Same non-negotiable constraint as task 025, confirmed true across every test file touched so far in this project: all admin test files (AdminDashboard.test.tsx, AdminCalendar.test.tsx, AdminAvailability.test.tsx, AdminServices.test.tsx, AdminLoginRequest.test.tsx, AdminLoginCallback.test.tsx) query exclusively via React Testing Library semantic queries (getByText/getByRole/getByLabelText/getByTestId), never CSS class or snapshot -- adding className attributes is safe, but existing visible text, ARIA roles, label associations, and data-testid values must not change. Mobile-first, per this project's established convention since task 018 -- verify at a narrow (phone-width) viewport, not desktop-first-then-adapted.
description: Extend the shared design system from task 025 to the remaining admin pages: AdminDashboard.tsx (including its List/Calendar/Availability/Services view toggle and the booking list with its Confirm/Decline/Cancel reveal-forms), AdminAvailability.tsx (the weekly-hours editor), AdminLoginRequest.tsx and AdminLoginCallback.tsx (currently fully unstyled, first-time treatment), and reconcile AdminCalendar.css/AdminServices.css's existing hardcoded colors/spacing to reference base.css's shared custom properties instead of their own separately-chosen values. The goal is one visually coherent app -- a masseur switching from the customer-facing preview to their own admin dashboard shouldn't feel like they've landed in a different, unstyled product.
acceptanceCriteria: AdminDashboard.tsx (view toggle, status filter, booking list, and the Confirm/Decline/Cancel reveal-forms) uses the shared design system consistently
AdminAvailability.tsx's weekly-hours editor (7 day rows, add/delete time-range rows, inline validation errors) uses the shared design system consistently
AdminLoginRequest.tsx and AdminLoginCallback.tsx are styled for the first time, consistent with the rest of the app
AdminServices.css's hardcoded color values are replaced with references to base.css's shared custom properties (or the file is removed entirely if everything it did is now covered by shared classes)

AdminCalendar.css's general UI chrome (toolbar, detail popup, buttons, spacing) references shared custom properties where it overlaps with what base.css already defines; the deliberate booking-status colors (pending/confirmed/blocked) are left untouched
All existing visible text, ARIA roles, label associations, and data-testid values are unchanged across every admin page -- only className/CSS is added
Every existing admin test suite (AdminDashboard, AdminCalendar, AdminAvailability, AdminServices, AdminLoginRequest, AdminLoginCallback) continues to pass unmodified
All admin pages verified usable and visually coherent at a narrow (phone-width) viewport
No new dependency added -- plain CSS only
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in frontend/ (backend should be unaffected since no backend files change)
relevantFilePaths: frontend/src/styles/base.css (existing shared design system -- read-only reference, the source of truth for tokens/classes to reuse)
frontend/src/pages/AdminCalendar.css (reconcile general chrome, preserve status colors)

frontend/test/AdminDashboard.test.tsx, AdminCalendar.test.tsx, AdminAvailability.test.tsx, AdminServices.test.tsx, AdminLoginRequest.test.tsx, AdminLoginCallback.test.tsx (must keep passing unmodified)
securityConsiderations: None -- purely visual/presentational change with no new data handling, no new API calls, and no change to any validation or business logic.
openQuestion: AdminCalendar.css already has a meaningful pending/confirmed color language (amber/green) that AdminDashboard.tsx's plain-text list view ('Status: pending') doesn't currently echo at all. Should this task extend that same status-color language to the list view too (e.g. a colored status badge/pill next to 'Status: pending'/'Status: confirmed'), for visual consistency between the two views of the same data -- or is that a new feature rather than 'polish,' better left for its own follow-up? Architect should weigh this and give a recommendation rather than silently including or excluding it.
